rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data or evaluator feedback, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract. Geometry: five line sensors at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m, spaced 20 mm so the 25 mm tape always covers at least one or two sensors. They sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the robot reads the line before it reaches it. Sensor size is 12 mm, which gives a clean reading across a 25 mm tape. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, body width 0.12 m (off-track limit about 0.06 m), body length 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg. Controller: sensor_weights = 25*x, giving -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1, so a line under the left sensors gives a positive signal (steer left) as the contract requires. kp = 4 gives roughly 1400 PWM per unit signal, enough steering authority for the sharper bends. ki = 0.05 is a small integral term to remove steady bias from the motor mismatch. kd = 0.05 damps overshoot without amplifying sensor noise. base_speed = 1.6 (about 80 percent of full PWM) is chosen to reach the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving headroom for turning. line_loss = last_direction, so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some slalom risk. Hypotheses to test: (1) the baseline completes all three tracks with few line-loss events; (2) completion time is near 2.5 s, meaning speed is adequate; (3) steering oscillation is low at kp = 4. Measurements requested below will show whether kp or base_speed is the bottleneck.
